hard_case: the edit drops a field, not only the identity, so the copy rule must not apply; the tested input already carries `ok: true`, so the structural pin cannot see the dropped field

truth.toolchain: node 22.22.0; jest 30.5.2, ts-jest 29.4.14, typescript 5.9.3; edit applied by hand and the test command run on the whole package

mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: an input with `ok: false` now comes back with `ok: false` instead of `true`; the only tested input already has `ok: true`, so both versions equal it

reasoning: `return { ...cfg, ok: true }` becomes `return { ...cfg }`. The test passes `cfg = { name: "bo", ok: true }` and asserts `expect(markOk(cfg)).toEqual(cfg)`, which passes on both versions; the test must hold on the stored package, so its input already carries `ok: true` and the dropped field cannot move the compared value. RIPR-SPEC-0246 example 3: the change is not copy-only, so rule 1 does not apply and the ladder's `exposed` stands. ripr reports `exposed`, as the spec states; against the not-discriminated truth that is a false exposed verdict the spec accepts.
